sec: Polyuria · definition, solute versus water diuresis and the causes of DI

items.q: Which absolute 24-hour urine volume defines polyuria on this page?
items.exp: Polyuria is defined three ways on this page: >40 mL/kg/day, >3 L/day and >2 L/m2. (Book p965)

items.q: Match each polyuria threshold with the denominator it uses — 1) >40 mL/kg/day 2) >3 L/day 3) >2 L/m2 … A) Body weight B) Fixed adult volume C) Body surface area
items.exp: The three definitions are per kilogram of body weight, an absolute adult figure of 3 L/day, and per square metre of body surface. (Book p965)

items.q: Assess against the three thresholds on Book p965: I A 60 kg adult passing 2.8 L/day is polyuric by the weight-based criterion. II A child passing 46 mL/kg/day is polyuric even if the absolute volume is under 3 L.
items.exp: 40 mL/kg/day of 60 kg is 2.4 L, so 2.8 L/day does cross the weight-based line; 46 mL/kg/day also exceeds the per-kilogram cut-off, which is exactly why the paediatric criterion exists. (Book p965)

items.q: The water-diuresis column of the comparison table carries which descriptor in brackets after its heading?
items.exp: The second column is headed 'Water diuresis (Hypotonic polydipsia)', in contrast with the solute-diuresis column. (Book p965)

items.q: All of the following appear in the causes row for solute diuresis EXCEPT:
items.exp: Solute diuresis is attributed to mannitol, glucose, relief of obstruction and long term diuretic use; psychogenic polydipsia sits in the water-diuresis column. (Book p965)

items.q: Fill up: In the water-diuresis column, central DI is ascribed to ______ deficiency and peripheral DI to ______ at the receptor.
items.exp: The column lists a. AVP (vasopressin) deficiency as central DI, b. AVP-r resistance as peripheral DI and c. psychogenic polydipsia. (Book p965)

items.q: The comparison table splits the two diuresis types by urine output. Which figure is used as the discriminator?
items.exp: Urine output below 7 L/day is placed with solute diuresis and above 7 L/day with water diuresis, even though polyuria itself starts at 3 L/day. (Book p965)

items.q: Match each table row with the value given for solute diuresis — 1) Urine osmolality 2) Urine dipstick 3) Urine output … A) Greater than 600 mosm/kg B) Positive C) Less than 7 L/day
items.exp: Solute diuresis shows urine osmolality above 600 mosm/kg, a positive dipstick and output under 7 L/day, whereas water diuresis shows osmolality below 300 mosm/kg, a negative dipstick, output above 7 L/day and specific gravity below 1.008. (Book p965)

items.q: Assess the last two rows of the table: I The specific-gravity row carries a value only in the water-diuresis column. II The dipstick is positive in water diuresis and negative in solute diuresis.
items.exp: Specific gravity is left as a dash under solute diuresis and given as <1.008 under water diuresis; the dipstick is the other way round, positive with solute diuresis and negative with water diuresis. (Book p965)

items.q: Two days after relief of a bilateral pelvic ureteric obstruction a patient passes 6 L/day; urine osmolality is 640 mOsm/kg and the dipstick is positive for glucose. Which column of the table does this picture belong to?
opts: Solute diuresis, since output is under 7 L/day with osmolality above 600
Water diuresis, since the volume exceeds 3 L/day
Central DI, since relief of obstruction damages the stalk
Psychogenic polydipsia, since the dipstick is positive
items.exp: Relief of obstruction is a named cause of solute diuresis, and the output below 7 L/day, osmolality above 600 mOsm/kg and positive dipstick all sit in that column. (Book p965)

items.q: Every item below belongs to the stalk-effect group of central DI EXCEPT:
opts: Infections such as tuberculosis and histoplasmosis
items.exp: The stalk-effect list covers tumor, infiltration, infections and lymphocytic hypophysitis, while Wolfram syndrome is filed under the autosomal recessive inherited group. (Book p965)

items.q: Which infiltrative trio is named under the stalk effect in central DI?
opts: Langerhans' cell histiocytosis, hemochromatosis and sarcoidosis
Hemochromatosis, metastatic breast deposit and histiocytosis X
items.exp: Infiltration is specified as Langerhans' cell histiocytosis, hemochromatosis and sarcoidosis; TB, HIV, histoplasmosis and toxoplasmosis form the separate infections list. (Book p965)

items.q: For inherited central DI, what is the sequence of inheritance modes as ranked on this page?
opts: Autosomal dominant before autosomal recessive before X-linked recessive
X-linked recessive before autosomal dominant before autosomal recessive
Autosomal recessive before X-linked recessive before autosomal dominant
Autosomal dominant before X-linked recessive before autosomal recessive
items.exp: The line reads AD > AR > XLR for inherited central DI. (Book p965)

items.q: Match each component of the Wolfram box with its numbered order of occurrence — 1) DM 2) OA 3) DI 4) Deafness … A) First B) Second C) Third D) Fourth
items.exp: The numbers under DI DM OA D read 3, 1, 2 and 4, so diabetes mellitus appears first, optic atrophy second, diabetes insipidus third and deafness fourth. (Book p965)

items.q: Fill up: The Wolfram box spells its four features as the letters ______, and the syndrome is inherited in the ______ pattern among central DI causes.
opts: DI, DM, OA, D; autosomal recessive
DI, DM, OD, A; X-linked recessive
DM, DI, DA, O; autosomal dominant
items.exp: DI, DM, OA and D are boxed as the four components, and the page lists Wolfram syndrome as the autosomal recessive form of inherited central DI. (Book p965)

items.q: Match each nephrogenic DI category with its examples — 1) Drugs 2) Metabolic 3) Autoimmune … A) Hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia and raised uric acid B) Lithium, demeclocycline, cisplatin, foscarnet, aminoglycosides, amphotericin B C) Sarcoidosis, Sjogren's and IgG4 disease
items.exp: The seven nephrogenic DI groups are drugs, sickle cell anaemia, pregnancy, metabolic, autoimmune, chronic tubulo-interstitial disease and inherited causes, with the entries matched as above. (Book p965)

items.q: Which of these agents is NOT among the drugs listed as causes of nephrogenic DI?
items.exp: The drug list is lithium, demeclocycline, cisplatin, foscarnet, aminoglycosides and amphotericin B; thiazides appear later in this chapter as treatment for nephrogenic DI. (Book p965)

items.q: In the metabolic group of nephrogenic DI, which trio of direction changes is recorded?
opts: Calcium up, potassium down, uric acid up
Calcium down, potassium up, uric acid down
Calcium up, potassium up, uric acid down
Calcium down, potassium down, uric acid up
items.exp: The metabolic row reads increased Ca2+, decreased K+ and increased uric acid as causes of nephrogenic DI. (Book p965)

items.q: Assess the inherited line for nephrogenic DI: I The page puts the X-linked form ahead of the autosomal recessive form. II The X-linked form is attributed to the aquaporin 2 gene and the recessive form to the V2 receptor gene.
items.exp: The ranking XLR > AR is correct, but the gene attribution is the reverse: the X-linked form is printed against the V receptor gene, written V_a on the page, while the autosomal recessive form is the aquaporin 2 gene. The X-linked defect is in the V2 receptor gene, the cAMP-coupled receptor of the collecting duct. (Book p965)

items.q: Pregnancy is explicitly listed as a cause in which of the two DI categories on this page?
items.exp: B. Pregnancy heads the second central DI group, and 3. Pregnancy reappears as the third cause in the nephrogenic DI list. (Book p965)
